title: Level up
summary: Turn Super Hopper into a game of three levels: a meadow, a cave and one you make yourself.
learn: make a game with three levels, each its own world
start every level the same way
show the level next to the score
win on the last level with if … else

chapters.title: Start
chapters.idea: Every level starts the same way.

chapters.title: Coins
chapters.idea: Clones stay in their own world.

chapters.title: Your level
chapters.idea: A copy is a quick start.

steps.title: Every level starts here
steps.text: A game with levels needs a start for each one. When a level starts, put the Hero on the left.
steps.why: Each level is a <<world>>. ((Events#hat:world|when any world starts)) runs when the game starts, and again each time a new level begins.

checklist.text: Inside, ((Motion#scene_go|move sprite Hero to x −128 y 40))

hints: In {{Events}}, find ((Events#hat:world|when any world starts)). It is near the bottom.
Put ((Motion#scene_go|move sprite Hero to x −128 y 40)) inside it. Pick Hero, and type −128 and 40.
steps.coach: The new “when” block is in Events.

steps.title: Next level, please
steps.text: The flag ends the game. Make it go to the next level instead!
steps.why: ((Game#scene_world_next|next world)) goes to the next <<world>> in the list: Level 1, then Level 2.

checklist.text: In ((Events#hat:overlap|when Hero overlaps Flag)), swap ((Game#game_finish|finish game win)) for ((Game#scene_world_next|next world))
Press [[Run code]] and reach the flag

hints: Pick Hero and find ((Events#hat:overlap|when Hero overlaps Flag)). Drag ((Game#game_finish|finish game win)) out of it, onto the palette.
From {{Game}}, put ((Game#scene_world_next|next world)) where it was.

predict.question: What will Level 2 look like?
choices: A dark cave with no coins and no beetles
Level 1 again, with all its coins
predict.explain: Level 2 is its own world, with cave tiles. The coins and beetles are <<clones|clone>>, and clones stay behind when the world changes.

steps.coach: Next world is in Game, under Levels.

steps.title: Show the level
steps.text: Show which level you are on, next to the score.
steps.why: The level is the world’s number: Level 1 is the first world in the list. It changes by itself when the world does.

checklist.text: Under ((Events#hat:start|when game starts)), add ((Game#game_show:FIELD=level|show level on HUD))

hints: In {{Game}}, under Levels, find ((Game#game_show:FIELD=level|show level on HUD)).
Snap it under ((Events#hat:start|when game starts)), with the score and lives.

steps.title: Coins in every level
steps.text: Level 2 has no coins and no beetles! Make them each time a level starts, not only once.
steps.why: <<Clones|clone>> belong to the world they were made in. ((Events#hat:world|when any world starts)) runs again in every level, so each level gets its own coins and beetles.

checklist.text: Move the coin and beetle blocks from ((Events#hat:start|when game starts)) into ((Events#hat:world|when any world starts))

hints: Find the ((Events#hat:start|when game starts)) that makes the coins. Drag its first block: the blocks under it come too.
Drop them inside ((Events#hat:world|when any world starts)), under ((Motion#scene_go|move sprite Hero to x −128 y 40)). Then drag the empty ((Events#hat:start|when game starts)) away.
steps.coach: Drag the first block: the rest come with it.

steps.title: Play: reach Level 2
steps.text: Play to the flag, and on into Level 2!
steps.why: Tap the game. [←] [→] walk and [space] jumps. Jump over the pits!

steps.title: A level of your own
steps.text: Make Level 3! Copy a level, then change it your way.
steps.why: The copy is called Level 3. Change its Backdrop, or paint new tiles: pick a Tile artwork, tick [[Solid]], and drag on the map.
hints: Open the [[Sprite tab]]. [[Worlds & tilemaps]] is under the stage settings.
Press [[Duplicate world]]. The copy is called Level 3, and Run starts there now.
steps.coach: Worlds & tilemaps is in the Sprite tab.

steps.title: The last level
steps.text: Run starts on Level 3 now. It is the last level. What will its flag do?
steps.why: After the last world, ((Game#scene_world_next|next world)) goes back to the first one, round and round.

checklist.text: Press [[Run code]] and reach the flag of Level 3

hints: Make your guess first. Then press [[Run code]] and play to the flag.
At the flag, ((Game#scene_world_next|next world)) runs. Which world comes after the last one?

predict.question: What happens at the flag of the last level?
predict.explain: There is no Level 4, so next world starts again at Level 1. The game needs to know when to stop!

steps.title: Win on the last level
steps.text: On Level 3, the flag should win the game. On the other levels, it goes on.
steps.why: <<if … else|if>> asks a question: is this Level 3? Yes: you win. No: next level.

checklist.text: In ((Events#hat:overlap|when Hero overlaps Flag)), use ((Control#controls_if:else|if … else)) to check if ((Game#game_get:FIELD=level|game level)) = 3

hints: From {{Control}}, put ((Control#controls_if:else|if … else)) inside ((Events#hat:overlap|when Hero overlaps Flag)). In its test, compare ((Game#game_get:FIELD=level|game level)) = 3.
Put ((Game#game_finish|finish game win)) in the first hole, and ((Game#scene_world_next|next world)) after else.

steps.title: Play all three levels
steps.text: Choose Level 1 in [[Starting world]], then play all three levels to win!
steps.why: The HUD shows the level. Reach the flag on Level 3 to win. Land on beetles from above!

finish.text: Three levels: a meadow, a dark cave and one you made yourself. Your game knows when it is over. Great work!
remix: Level 4: press [[Duplicate world]] again. Then the last level is 4, so change the 3 next to ((Game#game_get:FIELD=level|game level)) to 4.
Harder and harder: when a world starts, if ((Game#game_get:FIELD=level|game level)) is 3, make the beetles walk faster.
Your own look: give Level 3 the Snow backdrop and paint it with snow tiles.
